# Production Next.js Agent Rules (`AGENTS-nextjs.md`)

> Append this file to `AGENTS-frontend.md` in your Next.js project root as `AGENTS.md`.
> Next.js App Router (v14/v15) specific rules. Rules are annotated where behavior differs between versions — validate against your pinned version before adopting. Extends the universal frontend baseline — all rules in `AGENTS-frontend.md` remain in force. This file adds only Next.js-specific invariants. Append this block after the frontend rules in your combined `AGENTS.md` (frontend rules first, then these additions).

<!-- START AGENT-STANDARD: NEXTJS-PRODUCTION -->

## 1. React Server Components (RSC) Hygiene

- [ ] **Server Components by Default**: Every component MUST be a React Server Component unless it explicitly requires browser-only APIs, event handlers, or React hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, `useRef`, etc.). Do NOT add `'use client'` preemptively.
- [ ] **Push `'use client'` to the Leaves**: The `'use client'` directive MUST be placed as deep in the component tree as possible — on the smallest interactive leaf, never on layout or page shells. A `'use client'` boundary on a parent converts all its children to client bundles, defeating server rendering.
- [ ] **No Async Data Fetching in Client Components**: `async/await` data fetching MUST happen in Server Components or Route Handlers. Client Components MUST receive data via props from a Server Component parent or via a data-fetching cache (TanStack Query / SWR).
- [ ] **No Secret Leakage to Client Bundles**: Environment variables containing secrets MUST use server-only names (no `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix). The `server-only` package MUST be imported in any module that imports secrets or accesses server-side resources, to trigger a build error if accidentally imported client-side.
- [ ] **React Data Tainting for PII Models**: Projects handling sensitive data (user records, payment info, PII) SHOULD enable React's `taintObjectReference` and `taintUniqueValue` APIs (requires `experimental: { taint: true }` in `next.config.js`/`next.config.ts`). Apply tainting to raw database model objects containing passwords, tokens, or PII so that accidentally passing them from a Server Component to a Client Component throws a runtime error rather than silently leaking data to the browser. Note: these APIs remain experimental — pin the React/Next.js version and validate behavior on upgrade.

## 2. Routing, Navigation & URL Patterns

- [ ] **File-System Routing Conventions**: Route segments MUST follow Next.js App Router conventions — `page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `loading.tsx`, `error.tsx`, `not-found.tsx`. Non-route files (components, hooks, utils) MUST NOT be placed directly inside route segment directories; co-locate them in a `_components/` or `_lib/` folder within the segment or in a shared `src/` module.
- [ ] **Client-Side Navigation Only via `useRouter`**: All programmatic navigation in Client Components MUST use `useRouter().push()` / `useRouter().replace()` from `next/navigation`. Direct `window.location` assignments are strictly banned — they cause full page reloads and bypass Next.js client-side transitions. Note: `useRouter()` is a client-side hook — it MUST NOT be called in Server Components. For server-side redirects use `redirect()` from `next/navigation` instead.
- [ ] **URL Search Params as Authoritative State**: Shareable UI state (search filters, pagination, sort order, active tabs) MUST be read from and written to `searchParams` / `useSearchParams()`. Validate and parse search params using a typed schema (e.g. Zod or `nuqs`) — never access raw `searchParams` strings without validation.
- [ ] **Await `params` and `searchParams` in Next.js 15+**: In Next.js 15+, `params` and `searchParams` passed to page, layout, and `generateMetadata` functions are Promises. They MUST be awaited before accessing their properties: `const { slug } = await params`. Accessing `params.slug` synchronously (the Next.js 14 pattern) will produce deprecation warnings or errors. Use the official `@next/codemod` migration tool when upgrading.
- [ ] **Static Params Pre-generation**: Dynamic route segments with a small, bounded set of values SHOULD implement `generateStaticParams()` to pre-render pages at build time. For large datasets, generate only the highest-priority subset (e.g. top N by traffic) and rely on ISR (`dynamicParams = true`, the default) for on-demand generation of the remainder. Set `export const dynamicParams = false` explicitly only when pages outside the generated set should return 404. Do NOT call `cookies()`, `headers()`, or read `searchParams` inside `generateStaticParams` — it executes at build time only.
- [ ] **`next/link` Prefetch Management**: Use `<Link>` from `next/link` for all internal navigation — never bare `<a>` tags for client-side transitions. On pages rendering large lists of links (nav menus, paginated tables, search results), `prefetch={false}` SHOULD be set to prevent the router from issuing hundreds of simultaneous prefetch requests. Version note: **Next.js 14** prefetches all visible `<Link>` elements by default — `prefetch={false}` is the opt-out. **Next.js 15** only prefetches statically rendered routes by default — explicit `prefetch={true}` opts into aggressive prefetching. Match your config to your pinned version.

## 3. Rendering Strategy & Data Fetching

- [ ] **Rendering Strategy Decision Matrix**: Choose the correct rendering mode per route — Static Generation (SSG) for fully static content; Incremental Static Regeneration (`revalidate`) for semi-dynamic content with acceptable staleness; Server-Side Rendering (`dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`) only when data MUST be fresh at request time. Default to SSG/ISR over SSR.
- [ ] **Explicit `fetch()` Cache Semantics (Version-Sensitive)**: The default `fetch()` caching behavior differs by version — it MUST be declared explicitly on every call to avoid version-upgrade surprises. **Next.js 15+**: `fetch()` is uncached by default (`no-store`); opt into caching with `{ cache: 'force-cache' }` or `{ next: { revalidate: N } }`. **Next.js 14**: `fetch()` caches by default (`force-cache`); opt out with `{ cache: 'no-store' }`. Pin the project's expected version behavior in a project-level ADR so all agents apply the correct default.
- [ ] **`use cache` Directive for Expensive Operations**: For expensive data-fetching functions or component renders that should be cached across requests, use the `use cache` directive on the enclosing async function (Next.js 15+ preferred pattern over `unstable_cache`). Pair with `cacheLife` to define the cache profile (e.g. `cacheLife('hours')`) and `cacheTag` for granular invalidation. Existing `unstable_cache` usage SHOULD be migrated to `use cache` in Next.js 15+ projects.
- [ ] **Cache Invalidation on Mutations**: Server Actions or Route Handlers that mutate data MUST call `revalidatePath()` or `revalidateTag()` immediately after a successful write. Returning stale cached data after a user-triggered mutation is strictly forbidden.
- [ ] **Streaming with Suspense**: Pages with slow data dependencies MUST use React Suspense boundaries with `loading.tsx` or inline `<Suspense fallback={…}>` to stream progressive UI to the browser. Blocking the entire page render on a slow data fetch is strictly banned.
- [ ] **Third-Party Scripts via `next/script`**: All third-party scripts (analytics, chat widgets, tag managers, A/B testing tools) MUST be loaded using the `next/script` component with an explicit `strategy` prop. Dropping raw `<script>` tags into `layout.tsx` or `page.tsx` is strictly banned — they block the main thread and degrade INP. Use `strategy="afterInteractive"` for scripts that need DOM access, `strategy="lazyOnload"` for non-critical scripts, and `strategy="worker"` (via Partytown) only when the script is confirmed Partytown-compatible and the integration is tested.

## 4. Server Actions & Route Handlers

- [ ] **Zod Validation on Every Server Action**: All Server Action inputs MUST be validated against an explicit Zod schema before any business logic executes. Passing unvalidated `FormData` or raw objects to service/repository layers is strictly forbidden.
- [ ] **Server Action Authentication & Authorization Re-verification**: Every Server Action MUST independently verify that a valid authenticated session exists — do NOT rely solely on `middleware.ts` (middleware can be bypassed). For mutating actions on specific resources, the action MUST additionally verify that the authenticated user owns or has permission to modify the target resource (IDOR prevention). Server Actions are public POST endpoints reachable by anyone with the URL; treat them as untrusted at the boundary.
- [ ] **Rate Limiting on Sensitive Server Actions**: Server Actions that perform sensitive operations (authentication, account/password changes, bulk deletes, external message sends) MUST be protected by a rate limiter (e.g. Upstash Ratelimit, Arcjet, or equivalent) keyed on user ID or IP address.
- [ ] **Service Layer Delegation**: Server Actions and Route Handlers MUST NOT contain direct database queries or external API calls. All persistence logic MUST be delegated to the service/repository layer, keeping actions as thin transport orchestrators.
- [ ] **Route Handler Method Guards**: Route Handlers (`route.ts`) MUST export only the HTTP methods they handle (`GET`, `POST`, etc.) and return structured `NextResponse.json()` responses conforming to the project's unified error envelope (`code`, `message`, `details`, `timestamp`, `request_id`).
- [ ] **No Sensitive Operations in `GET` Handlers**: Data-mutating operations (writes, deletes, sends) MUST NOT be performed in `GET` Route Handlers. All mutations MUST use `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE` methods to prevent CSRF via prefetch/crawler requests.

## 5. Security Headers & Middleware

- [ ] **Security Headers via `next.config.js`/`next.config.ts`**: Production deployments MUST configure the `headers()` function in `next.config.js` (or `next.config.ts`, the default in Next.js 15+) to set: `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy`, and `Strict-Transport-Security`. Relying solely on hosting-platform defaults is insufficient.
- [ ] **Nonce-Based CSP for App Router**: The CSP MUST use a per-request nonce-based approach — generate a cryptographically random nonce in `middleware.ts`, forward it via a response header (e.g. `x-nonce`), and read it in Server Components via `headers()` to inject `<script nonce={nonce}>`. Static hash-based CSP MUST NOT be used as the sole mechanism — Next.js App Router generates dynamic inline scripts at runtime that cannot be whitelisted by build-time hashes.
- [ ] **Middleware as Optimistic Redirect Layer (Not Sole Auth Gate)**: `middleware.ts` MUST perform fast, edge-compatible authentication checks (JWT signature verification, session cookie existence) to redirect unauthenticated requests early as a performance optimization. This is an optimistic layer only — middleware can be bypassed (see CVE-2025-29927 class vulnerabilities). Ensure Next.js is patched to a version that mitigates known middleware bypass CVEs.
- [ ] **Data Access Layer (DAL) as Authoritative Auth Gate**: Server Components, Route Handlers, and Server Actions that access sensitive data MUST re-verify authentication and authorization in a centralized Data Access Layer (DAL) function, independent of middleware. Returning data based on middleware auth alone — without a DAL-level re-check — is strictly forbidden.
- [ ] **No Secrets in `NEXT_PUBLIC_` Variables**: Environment variables prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` are inlined into the client-side JavaScript bundle and visible to all users. API keys, service tokens, database URLs, and any credential MUST use server-only environment variables and be accessed exclusively in Server Components, Route Handlers, or Server Actions.

## 6. Testing Strategy (Next.js Additions)

- [ ] **Next.js Jest Configuration**: Tests MUST use the official `next/jest` transformer (`createJestConfig` from `next/jest`) to ensure Server Components, RSC transforms, and Next.js module aliases are correctly handled. Do NOT use a bare `ts-jest` or `babel-jest` config without Next.js integration.
- [ ] **Server Component Testing**: Server Components MUST be tested with Playwright E2E tests run against a production build (`next build && next start`) — this is the only approach that exercises the full RSC runtime, async data fetching, Next.js caching, and `cookies()`/`headers()` access. For simple, synchronous Server Components without data fetching, `react-dom/server` (`renderToString`) in integration tests is permitted as a lighter supplement. `@testing-library/react` alone MUST NOT be used for Server Components. Business logic inside Server Components SHOULD be extracted into pure functions and unit-tested with Jest/Vitest in isolation.
- [ ] **Route Handler Testing**: Route Handlers MUST have integration tests that exercise the full request/response cycle using `fetch()` against a running `next start` process or Playwright API testing. MSW-only interception MUST NOT be used as the sole Route Handler test strategy — it validates the mock, not the actual handler implementation.
- [ ] **No Mocking of Next.js Internals Without Cause**: Mocking `next/navigation` (`useRouter`, `useSearchParams`), `next/headers` (`cookies`, `headers`), or `next/cache` in Jest is only permitted when the component under test genuinely cannot be rendered in a Server Component or Playwright context. Every such mock MUST include a comment explaining why isolation is necessary.
